answer: Proof of unique storage: each identity must keep a large, randomly seeded chunk of data that is sealed to its own address, and peers send surprise challenges asking for a few random pieces within seconds. Like a river carving its own bed, each seal is slow to build and cannot be shared, so one disk cannot pass as many agents; an attacker running a thousand clones must buy a thousand times the storage. Viewed through that prism, the sybil cost scales linearly with clones, and an atlas of who answers on time shows which agents are real.
